name: OWASP Top 10 Privacy Risks
source_notes: IDs and titles from the owasp.org project page; type, frequency, impact and descriptions from tab_topprivacy.md in the OWASP GitHub repo.
caveats: The GitHub repo was archived (read-only) on 2025-03-15; treat the list as frozen.
Countermeasures exist only in a separate v2.0 PDF that was not read, so prevention is [] for all items.
P6 is "Insufficient Deletion of User Data" on the project page and "Insufficient Deletion of Personal Data" in tab_topprivacy.md.
There is no item literally named third-party data sharing; it falls under P2, P4, P5 and P10.
Frequency/impact scale: Low 0-1.5, Medium 1.5-1.9, High 1.9-2.3, Very High >2.3.
detection.static entries are reinhardt rule ideas inferred from the descriptions, not OWASP text.

items.name: Web Application Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Weaknesses in design, implementation, patching or detection of systems that hold user data put that data at risk; this includes the broader OWASP Top 10.

items.name: Operator-sided Data Leakage
items.summary: User data reaches unauthorized parties through malice or careless mistakes, typically due to weak access control, insecure storage, data duplication or poor training.

static: PII in logs (console.log/logger calls with password, token, email, req.body, req.headers.authorization)
PII or secrets in client bundles; user data sent to AI/LLM vendors
Over-permissive database rules (e.g. Supabase tables without RLS, open Firebase rules)

items.name: Insufficient Data Breach Response
items.summary: Failing to notify affected people, fix the root cause or contain damage after a breach.

items.name: Consent on Everything
items.summary: Consent is bundled across purposes instead of being collected separately for each one.

static: Analytics, advertising or session-replay SDKs initialized at app start with no consent gate
IDFA access without a prior requestTrackingAuthorization call (iOS)
A single consent toggle that enables several SDKs

items.name: Non-transparent Policies, Terms and Conditions
items.summary: Users are not given enough information about how their data is collected, stored and processed.

static: Third-party SDKs or data recipients found in code/manifests but not named in the privacy policy
Tag managers whose downstream recipients cannot be determined statically

items.name: Insufficient Deletion of User Data
items.summary: Personal data is not deleted effectively or in time once its purpose ends or the user asks.

items.name: Insufficient Data Quality
items.summary: Outdated, incorrect or bogus user data is used and not corrected.

items.name: Missing or Insufficient Session Expiration
items.summary: Sessions are not terminated effectively, which can lead to collecting more data without the user being aware.

static: Session cookies or JWTs with no expiry or a very long maxAge/expiresIn

items.name: Inability of Users to Access and Modify Data
items.summary: Users cannot access, change or delete data about them.

items.name: Collection of Data Not Required for the User-Consented Purpose
items.summary: More descriptive, demographic or other user data is collected than the purpose needs, or without proper consent.

static: SDKs or code collecting precise location, contacts, IDFA or device fingerprints beyond the stated purpose
Autocapture or session replay without input masking
Analytics track()/identify() calls carrying raw email or phone; PII sent to AI APIs
